# Frozen revision 9 reference-import note timing

This fixture isolates the compatibility import used by `NoteEvent.importReference`. It keeps every absolute onset and the existing format-1 endpoint serialization. Native `EventPlanner` events and their shared absolute clock are separate, unchanged contracts. The original 621-event JSON, acoustic fixtures, Python sources, and all existing sound tolerances remain unchanged.

The verifier extracts the actual original `render_room.voice`, `bass_voice`, and `place` expressions from their pinned Python AST. It evaluates those expressions against the original events, independently of Swift or C++ output. Guitar and piano round hold and release durations separately, then add their integer lengths. Bass rounds hold separately but rounds the combined duration-plus-release to obtain the complete oscillator length. Those are different at half-frame boundaries: 1.5 + 1.5 frames yields a four-frame harmonic span but a three-frame bass span; 2.5 + 0.5 yields two and three respectively. All rounding is the original nearest-even Python behavior on the supplied Double values.

Imported harmonic/bass gate and release endpoints are the preserved absolute onset plus those relative lengths. In this accepted score, 85 endpoint records differ from the former absolute-endpoint conversion: 58 guitar, 22 piano, and five bass. The manifest stores all 621 expected triples and each changed record's index and endpoint deltas. Endpoint acceptance is exact, with zero frame tolerance.

Fifteen additional raw-event probes include half-frame and zero-release cases, a guitar span extending beyond its recorded body, a bass oscillator extending beyond its recorded touch sample, four supported percussion one-shots, preserved absolute onset at a nonzero origin, and a zero-rounded-hold rejection. The verifier separately executes the unchanged original voice functions and traces their realized hold, source, and output lengths. Harmonic output clamps to the prepared sample length; bass output retains its complete oscillator span. Short and long gate/release inputs produce bit-identical original kick, stick-snare, closed-hat, and shaker PCM. Their unused serialized gate/release endpoints therefore retain the existing canonical conversion.

The positive-hold validity rule remains: a positive duration that rounds to zero is rejected instead of being extended by one frame. The original voice can construct a zero-hold diagnostic, but it is outside the typed import's accepted domain. The nonzero-origin probe locks the existing absolute-onset policy; it does not claim equivalence between local per-rack placement and subtracting an independently rounded absolute origin. That mapping remains future orchestration work.

`freeze-reference-timing.py` creates this independent expectation before implementation comparison and refuses replacement without explicit `--replace`. `verify-reference-timing.py --integrity` checks source provenance, inventory, schema, and probe definitions without DSP dependencies; its default mode additionally rederives all exact records and executes the original realized-length probes with the pinned reference environment. Swift tests compare imported records and codec round trips directly with this fixture. Existing full acoustic comparisons continue to use their original waveform goldens and limits. Full-song before/after comparisons must use the unchanged original signal, never the earlier endpoint-adjusted counterfactual.
